name: Aka / Baka forest forager polyphony (UNESCO 2003)
lineage: Central African Republic and southeastern Cameroon Aka / Baka / BaYaka rainforest hunter-gatherer four-and-more-part polyphonic vocal tradition recognized as UNESCO Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity 2003 — characterized by four canonical voice-parts in the Aka system (motangole the principal melodic voice, ngue-wa-lembo the equivalent of a bass anchor, osese the middle voice, and diyei the upper yodeled M1-M2-rapid-alternation voice with open vowels in M1 and closed/high vowels in M2), hocket interlocking single-note distribution across the ensemble, polyrhythmic-layered independent ostinato cycles per voice, and overlap-driven entrance-and-exit aesthetic; documented through the Simha Arom canonical ethnomusicological field-recording-and-analysis program (1970s-onward Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique France) and Susanne Fürniss yodel-mechanism phonetic analysis, with parallel Mbenga-Mbuti (Ituri Forest DRC pygmy-polyphonic tradition) related-but-distinct repertoire
